report.title: Multilingual Human Evaluation of Educational NLP Responses
report.research_question: RQ-MULTI-HUMAN: How do bilingual Telugu-English engineering students evaluate the correctness, grounding, and pedagogical clarity of answers generated across English, Telugu native script, Romanized Telugu, and code-mixed modalities?
report.hypothesis: IndicLearn maintains high factual grounding (>=4.0/5.0) across both English and Telugu modalities, with code-mixed explanations achieving higher perceived pedagogical clarity among bilingual students than purely translated technical Telugu.
report.procedure: Administer 4-modality comparative evaluation (en, te, te-Latn, te-en) across computer science concepts to bilingual engineering students, measuring correctness, grounding, naturalness, and technical terminology preservation.

report.interpretation: The multilingual human evaluation framework is established and disaggregated. Because real student evaluators have not yet been recruited, zero multilingual ratings are manufactured. The pipeline prevents conflating standard English performance with low-resource or code-mixed performance.
scientific_claims: The multilingual evaluation framework enforces strict disaggregation across English, Telugu, Romanized Telugu, and code-mixed settings to prevent masked degradation.
limitations: Automated retrieval and scope benchmarks (EXP-005A, EXP-005B) evaluate lexical/embedding retrieval, not human linguistic acceptability.
Romanized Telugu exhibits substantial dialectal and spelling variation across regional demographics.
Empirical conclusions require formal execution with enrolled engineering students under approved IRB protocol.
